Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 1–2:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat Ḥā Mīm ʿAyn Sīn Qāf (Sūrat Ḥā Mīm ʿAsaqa)

It is Meccan.

(Muqatil said): except His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is what Allah gives good news of to His servants who believe﴾ — the verse — and likewise His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who, when an oppression afflicts them, they defend themselves﴾.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Ḥā Mīm ʿAyn Sīn Qāf﴾. ʿIkrima related from Ibn ʿAbbas that Alif Lam Rā, Ḥā Mīm, and Nūn form the arrangement of the word "al-Raḥmān" (the Most Gracious). It is also related from al-Ḥasan and Qatada that it is one of the names of the Qur'an. And it is related from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi: the Ḥāʾ is from "al-Ḥalīm" (the Forbearing), the Mīm is from "al-Malik" (the King), the ʿAyn is from "al-ʿĀlim" (the All-Knowing), the Sīn is from "al-Quddūs" (the Most Holy), and the Qāf is from "al-Qādir" (the All-Powerful). It is related from some of them that this is an oath, as if He swore by His forbearance, His kingship, His knowledge, His loftiness, and His power. Ḍaḥḥāk related from Ibn ʿAbbas that "Ḥā Mīm ʿAyn Sīn Qāf" is the Greatest Name of Allah. Ibn Masʿud and Ibn ʿAbbas read "Ḥā Mīm Sūq" without the ʿAyn. It is related from Ḥudhayfa, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: its meaning is "a punishment has passed, which is going to occur." It was also said: the Ḥāʾ indicates a war that will occur, the Mīm a transfer of kingship from one people to another, the ʿAyn an enemy that will overcome the Arabs, after which the dominion will belong to the Arabs, the Sīn is [sanaw] famine, and the Qāf is the all-penetrating power of Allah over the kings of the earth. In the Tafsir of al-Naqqash: the letters of the alphabet at the beginning of this surah are a sign of trials that will occur in this community. He said: ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, used to teach them and judge by them. His saying: ﴿Thus﴾ — in the tafsir: that "Ḥā Mīm ʿAyn Sīn Qāf" was revealed to every prophet among the prophets.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿Thus does He reveal to you﴾, meaning: just as Allah, exalted is He, revealed these words to the prophets, so He reveals them to you. It is also said: what is meant by it is revelation in general.

And His saying: ﴿And to those before you—Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾, meaning: Allah, exalted is He, reveals to you and to those before you, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. That is, from His attributes are might and wisdom. Its meaning is: Mighty in His victory, Wise in His actions. It has been recited as: "Thus do We reveal to you" with the nun, and its meaning is known.
The words of the Most High: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The heavens are almost torn apart from above them﴾. It is also read "yanfaṭirna" (ينفطرن), and its meaning is: they split (yatashaqqaqna).

His saying: ﴿from above them﴾, meaning: from above the earths. Their splitting is due to the magnitude of what the disbelievers have uttered. It is also said: out of fear of God, the Exalted. And it is said: out of awe and veneration. It is also said: due to the greatness of God, the Exalted.

His saying: ﴿And the angels glorify the praise of their Lord﴾, meaning: they pray with the praise of their Lord. And it is said: they declare their Lord free of imperfection (tanzih).

His saying: ﴿and they seek forgiveness for those on the earth﴾, meaning: for the believers who are on the earth. This is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. The wording is general but what is intended is specific (ʿāmm urīda bihi al-khāṣṣ). It is also said that those who seek forgiveness for the believers are specifically the bearers of the Throne, as mentioned by God, may He be exalted, in Surah al-Mu'min. And it is said: they are all the angels. In the exegesis it is reported that their seeking forgiveness for those on the earth dates from the time when Harut and Marut were tempted by the woman called Zuhrah, and they did what they did and chose the punishment of this world. Before that time the angels used to call down curses upon the sinners, but from that time onward they began to seek forgiveness for the sinful among the believers.

His saying: ﴿Surely God, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾, meaning: the Concealer of the sins of His servants.

His saying: ﴿the Merciful﴾, meaning: Merciful towards them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 6:

Allah's saying, ﴿And those who take protectors other than Him﴾: that is, protectors other than Allah.

And His saying, ﴿Allah is Watchful over them﴾: that is, Witness to their deeds and Guardian of them, so that He may recompense them for them.

And His saying, ﴿And you are not a guardian over them﴾: that is, not one who has authority over them. This was before the revelation of the verse of the sword.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 7:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you﴾ has already been explained earlier.

And His saying: {That you may warn the Mother of the Cities}, that is, the people of the Mother of the Cities. It is Makkah, and it was called the Mother of the Cities because the earth was spread out from beneath it.

And His saying: ﴿and those around it﴾, meaning: and you may warn the people around it.

And His saying: ﴿and warn of the Day of Assembly﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, which is the day on which the people of the heavens and the people of the earth will be gathered. It was also said: on it the first and the last will be gathered. Its meaning is: that you may warn about the Day of Assembly.

And His saying: ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾, meaning there is no doubt about its coming.

And His saying: ﴿a party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze﴾. Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out one day with two books in his hand, then said to his companions: "Do you know what is in them?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said to the book that was in his right hand: "This is a book containing the names of the people of Paradise and the names of their fathers, summarized up to the last of them; nothing will be added to them and nothing will be subtracted." He said to the book that was in his left hand: "This is a book containing the names of the people of the Fire and the names of their fathers, summarized up to the last of them; nothing will be added to them and nothing will be subtracted." They said: "Then what should we do?" He said: "Act, for whoever is among the people of Paradise will be concluded with the deeds of the people of Paradise, and whoever is among the people of the Fire will be concluded with the deeds of the people of the Fire, whatever deed he may do." Then he said: "Your Lord has finished with His creation: a party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze."

In the exegesis it is said: they will be scattered in the Garden and the Blaze, so they will never be gathered together again.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 8:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made them one community﴾, meaning: people of one religion.

And His saying: ﴿But He admits whom He wills into His mercy﴾, meaning: He admits whom He wills into Islam.

And His saying: ﴿But the wrongdoers have no protector or helper﴾, meaning: no protector who intercedes for them, and no protector who defends them from the punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 9:

Allah's saying: ﴿Or have they taken protectors besides Him?﴾ That is: Rather, they have taken protectors besides Allah.

And His saying: ﴿But Allah, He is the Protector﴾ That is: He is the one who takes charge of (lit. "who is in charge of," al-mutawalli) all things.

And His saying: ﴿And He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things Competent﴾ its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whatever you differ about, its judgment is with God﴾. Those who reject analogy (qiyas) in new matters have taken proof from this verse. He said: "The judgment belongs to God, not to the opinion of men." The Kharijites used to say the same: "There is no judgment but God's," and they rejected the two arbitrators. This argument, however, is unsound. For according to us, whoever holds to analogy (qiyas) and independent reasoning (ijtihad) is in fact returning to God regarding His ruling, since the foundations of analogical reasoning are: the Book, and the Sunnah.

And His saying: ﴿That is God, my Lord; in Him I have put my trust, and to Him I turn in repentance﴾. That is: in Him I have trusted, and to Him I return in my affairs.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: Creator of the heavens and the earth.

His saying: ﴿He has made for you, from yourselves, mates﴾, meaning: women. It was also said: "from yourselves, mates" means kinds, males and females.

And His saying: ﴿and of the cattle, mates﴾, meaning: kinds, males and females.

And His saying: ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾. Al-Farra' said: meaning, He increases you through it. Mujahid said: offspring after offspring, of humans and animals, until the Hour arrives. There is another view regarding the verse: that the meaning of His saying ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾ is that He creates you in this manner which He has mentioned.

And His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾. Tha'lab said: "There is nothing like Him" (laysa kahuwa shay'), and many of the grammarians claimed that the kaf (ka-, "like") here is superfluous, and its meaning is: "There is nothing like Him" (laysa mithluhu shay'). Some of them claimed that the dialect of Tihama is that they say: "I am like you" (ana kamithlika) or "you are like me" (anta kamithli), meaning: you are like me and I am like you. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: the statement of whoever says "there is nothing like His like" (laysa kamithlihi mithl) is not sound, because in this there is (an affirmation) of a likeness, and God, exalted is He, is not described with a likeness, exalted and high is He above that.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾, its meaning is apparent. And they cited poetry in support of the first view:

(Sa'd ibn Zayd, when you see their excellence... there is none among people like them.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 42, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿To Him belong the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth﴾. Concerning maqalid there are two opinions. The first: that it is Persian, and that it is al-akalid, whose singular is iklid (ikleed). The second opinion, which is the more sound (al-asahh), is that it is Arabic. The poet said regarding maqalid: (A youth who, if the sun were to call out, would cast off her veil, or the traveling moon would cast off its keys [maqalid]).

The opinions differ concerning the meaning of maqalid. Some said: the keys of the heavens are the rains, and the keys of the earth are the varieties of plants. It was also said: the keys of the heavens and the earth are the springs within them. It was also said: they are what He brings into being by His will. In some reports from Ibn 'Umar, the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning the keys of the heavens and the earth: "There is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, I seek the forgiveness of Allah, and there is no power and no strength except by Allah. He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, in His hand is the good, He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things powerful. Whoever says them is protected from Iblis and his soldiers."

His saying: ﴿He enlarges the provision for whom He wills and restricts it﴾, i.e., He widens provision for whom He wills and constricts it for whom He wills.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of all things﴾, i.e., Knowing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 13:

Allah's words, ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion﴾, meaning: He has made clear to you of the religion. Shar' (ordinance, legislation) is bayan (clarification), and it is said: He has manifested it to you and commanded you.

His words, ﴿that which He enjoined upon Nuh﴾, meaning: He commanded Nuh with it. It is said that Nuh, peace be upon him, was the first to bring the prohibition of mothers, sisters and daughters.

His words, ﴿and that which We revealed to you﴾, meaning: and the ordinance which We revealed to you.

His words, ﴿and that which We enjoined upon Ibrahim, Musa and Isa﴾, meaning: and that which We commanded Ibrahim, Musa and Isa.

His words, ﴿Establish the religion﴾, meaning: remain steadfast upon tawhid (the oneness of God). It is also said: "Establish the religion" means: be upright in the religion. It is said: "Establish the religion" is the performance of acts of obedience and compliance with the commands.

His words, ﴿and do not be divided therein﴾, meaning: as the Jews and Christians divided, i.e., they believed in some and disbelieved in others.

His words, ﴿Grievous to the polytheists is that to which you invite them﴾, meaning: what you invite them to, of tawhid, was great and weighty in the eyes of the polytheists. This is the meaning of Allah's words: ﴿Has he made the gods a single God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾

His words, ﴿Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills﴾, meaning: He selects for His religion whom He wills.

His words, ﴿and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾, meaning: He guides to returning to Him whoever chooses rectitude and repentance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they did not divide except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾. He means: the Jews and the Christians. And His saying: ﴿out of envy among themselves﴾, i.e., out of jealousy among themselves.

And His saying: ﴿And had it not been for a word that had preceded from your Lord﴾. The people of tafsir said: the word that preceded from God is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾.

And His saying: ﴿until a specified term, the matter would have been decided between them﴾, i.e., the matter would have been settled between them immediately. ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them﴾, i.e., after those who came before them. And His saying: ﴿were given﴾, i.e., were granted it.

And His saying: ﴿are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So for that, call (them)﴾, meaning: so to this, call, and this is the Tawhid (Oneness of God). Al-Nahhas mentioned that in the verse there is an inversion of order (taqdim wa ta'khir), and its meaning is: what you call the polytheists to has been hard for them; so for that, call [i.e.] to that. The preposition lam may also be used with the meaning of ila (to), as the poet said: "Awha laha al-qarar fa-staqarrat" ("He inspired her to settle, and she settled"), i.e., awha ilayha (he inspired to her).

His saying: ﴿And be steadfast as you have been commanded﴾ has already been explained.

His saying: ﴿And do not follow their desires﴾, meaning: the desires of the disbelievers.

His saying: ﴿And say: I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down﴾, meaning: the Torah, the Gospel, the Qur'an and all the other books.

His saying: ﴿And I have been commanded to do justice between you﴾, meaning: to judge between you with justice.

His saying: ﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord﴾, meaning: our Creator and your Creator.

His saying: ﴿For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds﴾, meaning: for us is the reward of our deeds, and for you is the reward of your deeds.

His saying: ﴿There is no argument between us and you﴾, meaning: there is no disputation between us and you. Among their arguments was that they said: "Our prophet came before your prophet, and our Book came before your book." The meaning of His saying ﴿there is no argument between us and you﴾ is: there is no (argument) for you, because Allah, exalted is He, has refuted your argument. When their argument is refuted, no disputation remains between them and the believers.

His saying: ﴿Allah will gather us together﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection.

His saying: ﴿And to Him is the final return﴾, meaning: to Him is the place of return.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 42, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who dispute concerning God﴾, meaning: they argue against God (يُخَاصِمُونَ فِي الله). We have already explained their argument that they clung to. Disputing concerning God means that they used to say: "We have a better claim to God than you." This is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿These two adversaries who dispute concerning their Lord﴾.

His saying: ﴿after it has been responded to﴾, meaning: after the believers responded to the Messenger.

His saying: ﴿their argument is baseless﴾, meaning: false.

His saying: ﴿with their Lord, and upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment﴾. We have explained this before. If it is said: He said, "after it has been responded to," so what is the meaning of people's responding to him in this context, when their argument is baseless whether or not people responded to him? The answer: the disbelievers thought that the affair of Muhammad would soon vanish and that matters would return to what they were upon, and that people would not respond to him or enter his religion. So He mentioned "after it has been responded to," meaning: people have responded to him, and your assumption that his affair would soon vanish has been nullified. This is the best benefit. There is another view: that His saying "after it has been responded to" means: after God responded to what was requested of Him concerning the manifestation of miracles upon him. It is related from some of them that disputing with falsehood is supporting a corrupt belief, and supporting a corrupt belief occurs in two ways: by presenting a doubt, and by repelling a proof without any proof.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 17:

The words of God Most High: ﴿It is Allah who has sent down the Book with truth﴾, meaning: He sent down the Qur'an with command and prohibition, reward and punishment.

And His words: ﴿and the Balance﴾, meaning: justice. Justice was called a balance (mizan) because the balance establishes equity (munasafa) among people in their dealings with one another. It is also said that it is the physical balance itself. The meaning of "sending down" is that God Most High sent down iron from the sky, and from the iron came the beam (lisan) of the balance and its pans (sanajat).

And His words: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾. If it is asked: why did He say "qarib" and not "qariba," when the word "al-sa'a" (the Hour) is feminine? The answer: the feminine form of "al-sa'a" is not real (haqiqi), because it means time and moment. It is also possible that "al-sa'a" means the Resurrection and the rising up, in which case the masculine form refers to the meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 18:

And His saying: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾. In the tafsir (explanation) it is said: the disbelievers used to come to the Prophet and ask him about the Hour, when it would occur, and they would say: "Why do you not ask your Lord to establish it now?" Some of them would say: "O Allah, if we are upon falsehood, then establish the Hour upon us." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

And His saying: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾: their seeking to hasten it was by way of deeming it far-off, denying it.

His saying: ﴿And those who believe are apprehensive of it﴾, that is, they are fearful and anxious of it, and their fear is of the promised reckoning and the recompense that falls upon their deeds.

And His saying: ﴿and know that it is the truth﴾, that is, that it will certainly be established.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in far error﴾, that is, they doubt it. It was also said: they dispute about it with the dispute of doubters.

And His saying: ﴿are in far error﴾, that is, in a long-standing mistake.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah is Gentle with His servants﴾, meaning: Kind (barr) and Compassionate (rahim) toward them. It is also said that the meaning of al-Latif (the Gentle) here is al-Razzaq (the Provider), meaning: He does not let them perish from hunger, but provides for them. Some scholars have said: the intended meaning of "His servants" wherever it is mentioned is the believers specifically, and the pronoun is for idafah (possessive attachment), while the preposition ba' of specification (ba' al-takhsis) necessitates and requires this.

And His saying: ﴿And He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty﴾, meaning: the Strong in aiding the believers. It is also said: the Strong in the power to deliver provision to them. And His saying: ﴿al-Aziz (the Mighty)﴾, meaning: the Overpowering who cannot be overpowered.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, that is, works for the Hereafter. From this is the saying of Abdullah ibn Amr, and it is said [it is] Ibn Mas'ud: "Cultivate for your worldly life as though you will live forever, and cultivate for your afterlife as though you will die tomorrow."

And His saying: ﴿We increase for him in his tilth﴾, that is, We multiply for him the good deeds. It is related from Qatadah that he said: "Indeed Allah, exalted is He, gives the world in return for the deeds of the Hereafter, but He does not give the Hereafter in return for the deeds of the world." This is a second view regarding the meaning of the verse. The third view is that the meaning of the verse: ﴿We increase for him in his tilth﴾, that is, We help him [and enable him] to increase acts of obedience and to abound in them.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world﴾, that is, the deeds of this world, ﴿We give him of it﴾, that is, according to what We will and wish, as He said in another verse: ﴿Whoever desires the hastening [world], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We desire.﴾ It is also said: "We give him of it according to what has been decreed for him."

And His saying: ﴿And he has no share in the Hereafter﴾. This is regarding one who works only for the world. As for one who works for both the world and the Hereafter, it is permissible that Allah grants him both the world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 21:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do they have partners﴾, meaning: rather, do they have partners?

And His saying: ﴿who have instituted for them in religion﴾, meaning: they have laid down (shara'u, "instituted").

And His saying: ﴿that for which Allah has not given permission﴾, meaning: that which Allah has not commanded.

And His saying: ﴿And had it not been for the decisive word﴾, meaning: what He has deferred for them of the punishment (law-qudiya baynahum), meaning: the matter would have been settled between them immediately.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment﴾, meaning: severe.

You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, and it will befall them (Q 42:22). Its meaning: the punishment they fear is descending upon them, and this is the Day of Resurrection.

His words: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in the meadows of the gardens﴾. That is, the gardens (al-basatin).

His words: ﴿They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty﴾. That is, the great (al-'azim).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 23:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is what Allah gives good news of to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, meaning: this is what Allah gives good news of to His servants.

And His saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the near of kin﴾. Regarding this there are four opinions. The most apparent and well-known of them is that its meaning is: I do not ask you anything except that you love me because of my kinship with you. It was also said: that you maintain the kinship that is between me and you by responding to me in what I call to, and that you restrain your harm from me. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, which al-Bukhari transmitted from him in the Sahih with a known and accepted wording, and it is the saying of Tawus, Mujahid, Qatadah, and the majority of the exegetes (mufassirun). Qatadah said: "The Quraysh used to maintain the ties of kinship, so the Prophet asked them to maintain the kinship that is between him and them, and not to sever it."

And from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: "There is no clan (batn) of the clans of Quraysh except that the Messenger of Allah has kinship among them, so he asked them to maintain it."

The second opinion: what is related from al-Hasan al-Basri, that he said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the near of kin﴾ means: that they should show affection toward Allah by what brings them near to Him of righteous deeds.

The third opinion: what is related from al-Dahhak, that the verse is abrogated (mansukhah) by His saying: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours; my reward is only with Allah﴾. This opinion is not accepted by the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani), because His saying ﴿except love for the near of kin﴾ is not a true exception such that it would contradict His saying ﴿my reward is only with Allah﴾; rather it is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), and its meaning is: Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, meaning wealth, and the speech is complete. And the meaning of His saying ﴿except love for the near of kin﴾ is: but maintain my kinship by responding to me, or restrain your harm from me.

In some exegeses it is mentioned that when the people of the pre-Islamic era (jahiliyyah) knew the dignity (jadd) of the Prophet, they thought he was seeking wealth, so they gathered for him a fine amount of their property and said: "We will give you this wealth, and you will refrain from what you are upon." So Allah revealed the verse in the sense we have mentioned earlier.

The fourth opinion: what is narrated in some rare reports, by the transmission of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas, that the meaning of His saying ﴿except love for the near of kin﴾ is that you should love my relatives and be affectionate toward them.

And some have related that the Prophet was asked about this, and about the meaning of "the near of kin," and he said: "'Ali, Fatimah, and their two sons." This is the most strange and weakest of the opinions.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever commits a good deed﴾, meaning: earns a good deed, that is, an act of obedience, ﴿We increase for him therein good﴾, meaning: We multiply the good deed for him.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾, meaning: Forgiving of many sins, Appreciative of small acts of obedience.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"?﴾ That is: they say about Allah what He has not said and has not sent down.

And His saying: ﴿If Allah willed, He would seal up your heart﴾ That is: He would cause you to forget the Qur'an, so that you would not recall a single letter of it. This was said by Qatadah. The second opinion: "He would seal up your heart" means He would bind it with patience in the face of their harm. This is a well-known view, cited by al-Farra' (a grammarian and exegete), al-Zajjaj (a grammarian and exegete) and others.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah will efface falsehood﴾ It has been said: this is the beginning of a new statement, and its meaning is: Allah will erase disbelief and remove it.

And His saying: ﴿And establish the truth by His words﴾ That is: He will support His religion through the miracles He manifests. It has also been said: by fulfilling His promise. And it has been said: by supporting His Messenger by making His religion prevail over all religions.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ That is: of what is in the breasts.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 25:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds﴾, i.e., sins, ﴿and knows what you do﴾, i.e., what you perform.

It is established from the Prophet (ﷺ), by the narration of al-Zuhri, from [Abu] Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than any one of you who loses his camel in a desert wasteland, with his provisions and his food on it, then searches for it and cannot find it. Then he lies down to sleep and wakes up to find it beside his head."

The Shaykh, the Imam, said: Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad informed us; Abu Sahl Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Razi informed us; Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Udhafiri informed us; Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dabari informed us, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, the report.

And from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) that he was asked about a man who committed fornication with a woman and then married her, whether it is permissible. He said: Yes, and he recited the words of the Most High: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ to the end of the verse.

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And He answers those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, meaning: He responds to their supplication.

And His words: ﴿and gives them increase from His bounty﴾, meaning: a good reputation in this world. It is also said: intercession in the Hereafter. And the well-known (view) is the multiplication of good deeds.

And His words: ﴿As for the disbelievers, there is a severe punishment for them﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 27:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah were to expand provision for His servants﴾, meaning: He would make their provision abundant. It was also said: He would give them everything they wish for.

And His saying: ﴿they would surely transgress in the earth﴾, meaning: they would disobey and act arrogantly in the earth. Transgression (al-baghy) in the earth is acting in it without right, and it was said that it is wantonness (al-batar) and insolence (al-ashar).

And His saying: {But He sends down in measure what He wills}, meaning: in measure as He wills.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is Acquainted with His servants, Seeing﴾, meaning: Acquainted with what sets them right, Seeing what they do and what they seek.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired﴾, i.e., they had lost hope (qanaṭū, "they despaired"). And in some reports it is related that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the land has become barren and the people have despaired, so pray to Allah that He send down rain for us." So he (ﷺ) said to him: "Return to your people, for you have been given rain." And it was as he said.

﴿And spreads His mercy﴾, i.e., by sending down the rain.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy﴾, i.e., the Owner of what He does, the one deserving praise for what He sends down of rain.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 29:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and what He has scattered within them of living creatures﴾ — regarding this there are two opinions.

The first: that what is meant is "and what He has scattered on the earth of living creatures." So He mentions the heaven and the earth, while only one of them is meant, and this is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿From both of them come forth pearls and coral﴾, whereas they are extracted only from one of them, namely the salt water, not the sweet.

The second opinion: that His saying, ﴿and what He has scattered within them of living creatures﴾, is to be taken in its literal sense, and "dabbah" (living creature, that which crawls or moves) is everything that moves, and the angels are among those that move. This was said by Mujahid and others.

﴿And He is able to gather them whenever He wills﴾ — that is, Capable (qadir).

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned; and He pardons much.﴾ If someone says: "We see one who is struck by an affliction without any sin having preceded from him, so what is the meaning of the verse?" The answer comes in several aspects.

The first: the words ﴿whatever affliction befalls you﴾ refer to the hudud (legal punishments) that are enforced, which are applied only to the one who disobeys, and are not applied to the obedient. This is a good view.

The second: the words ﴿whatever affliction befalls you﴾ are intended to mean punishment for what your hands have earned. According to this, it is permissible for a person to be struck by an affliction without sin or earning, when it is not intended as punishment.

The third view: the verse is general, and Allah does not afflict anyone with trial or hardship except for a sin that preceded from him, or as a warning so that he does not commit a sin, or so that the one with sin may take a lesson from it.

It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no scratch, nor a stumble of the foot, nor a twitching of a vein, except for a sin; and what Allah forgives is more." And it is related from al-'Ala' ibn Badr: "No affliction befalls anyone except because of a sin from him." It was said to him: "How is this, when you became blind as a child, and you were not blind [before]?" He said: "Because of the sin of my father."

Some who hold the doctrine of metempsychosis (tanasukh) have clung to this verse and said: "We see trials striking children, though no sin came from them, so this shows that sins preceded from them in earlier [lives] and they were punished for them."

Also, some who say that children do not feel pain at all, and likewise animals, and that their crying is only due to the distress of their parents' hearts, have clung to this verse.

Both views are false. According to the People of the Sunnah, it is permissible that Allah creates pain upon whomever He wills of His servants without any sin having preceded from them, and likewise upon all animals. As for the meaning of the verse, we have explained it. Likewise, the saying of one who claims that children do not feel pain is false, because it contradicts what is perceived by the senses and observed.

And His saying: ﴿And you cannot escape [Allah] on earth﴾ — that is, you cannot escape Allah on earth. We have already explained its meaning earlier.

And His saying: ﴿And you have no protector or helper apart from Allah﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs are the ships gliding through the sea like mountains﴾. That is, the ships (sufun). And His saying: ﴿like mountains﴾ means: like mountains. Al-Khansa' said, praising her brother Sakhr:

(Indeed Sakhr, the guides take their direction by him, as if he were a landmark (alam) with a fire atop it.)

That is: a mountain.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 33:

His words: ﴿If He wills, He stills the wind﴾ mean: if He wills to still the wind, the wind becomes still. Qatadah said: "Ships run by the winds; when the winds blow, they sail, and when they become still, they stand still."

His words: ﴿so they remain motionless on its back﴾ mean: stationary on the surface of the sea. Its meaning is: when the wind becomes still, the ships remain stationary on the surface of the sea, not moving.

His words: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful one﴾ mean: steadfast in the face of trials, grateful for blessings. It is related from some of them that ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful one﴾ means the believer, because the believer is the steadfast and grateful one. Mutarrif said: "How excellent is the believing servant: when he is tested, he is patient, and when he is given, he is grateful." And ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allah said: "How many a one bestowed upon is not grateful, and how many a one tested is not patient."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or He causes them to perish because of what they have earned﴾ means: He destroys the ships with those who are in them. It is also said: the people of the ships. And His saying: ﴿because of what they have earned﴾ means: because of the sins they have earned. And His saying: ﴿Or﴾ means: or, if He wills, He causes them to perish.

And His saying: ﴿and pardons much﴾ means: He overlooks many of the sins. It is related that Shurayh (al-Qadi) was seen with a boil (qarha) on his hand, and it was said to him: "What is this, Abu Umayyah?" He said: "And whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much."

And His saying: ﴿And those who dispute concerning Our signs will know﴾. It has been recited as "wa-yaʿlama" with a ḍamma on the mīm. As for the recitation with a fatḥa on the mīm, it is by the implied "an" (that), and as for the recitation with a ḍamma (raf‘) on the mīm, its meaning is: "and those who dispute concerning Our signs will know."

﴿They will have no place of escape﴾. That is: refuge and a place to flee to; this was said by al-Suddi and others.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 36:

And His saying: ﴿So whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ means: the benefit of the worldly life.

And His saying: ﴿But what is with Allah is better and more lasting﴾ means: the Garden is better and more enduring.

And His saying: ﴿For those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾ its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 37:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who avoid the major sins (kaba'ir al-ithm) and the abominations﴾. It is also read "kabir al-ithm" (the singular). We have already explained the meaning of the kaba'ir (major sins) earlier.

In the tafsir it is related that killing a soul, slandering chaste women, associating partners with God, disobedience to one's parents, fleeing from the battlefield, consuming the property of orphans, uttering "uff" (a word of contempt toward parents), sorcery, and drinking wine are among the major sins. It is also said: everything for which God has threatened punishment in the Fire is one of the major sins. As for the attribution of the major sins to ithm (sin), it is said: He attributed them to it only because within sin there is both major and minor. And it is said: the attribution of the major sins to sin is like the attribution of a quality to the thing it describes.

His saying: ﴿and the abominations﴾. The fawahish (abominations) are the vile deeds, such as fornication and other things.

His saying: ﴿and when they are angry, they forgive﴾, i.e., they overlook. In the well-known report, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Shall I tell you who is the strong one?" They said: "Yes." He said: "The one who controls himself at the time of anger."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 42, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who answer their Lord⌋﴾. It is said that the verse was revealed concerning the Ansar, and it is also said that it is general.

And His saying: ﴿and establish the prayer﴾. Establishing the prayer means performing it with its conditions and preserving it within its limits.

And His saying: ﴿and their affair is by consultation among themselves﴾. al-Naqqash (al-Naqqash) mentioned that this refers to the Ansar, who would consult one another about their affairs; so Allah praised them for that. This is evidence for unity of word, for abandoning arbitrary autocracy in opinion, and for returning to consultation when an incident occurs. It is also said that the Ansar consulted among themselves when the Prophet invited them to faith, and then they answered the call to faith.

From al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: "No people consult together except that they are guided to the best of their affairs." The word shura (consultation) is derived from their saying: "I shurtu the animal, ashuruha," meaning when I make it move forward and backward to extract its paces from it. It is said that the place for that is called al-mishwar. The Arabs say: "Beware of the matter (al-khatb), for it is a place of much obstinacy." In a report transmitted by Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When your rulers are your best, your wealthy are your most generous, and your affairs are by consultation among you, then the surface of the earth is better for you than its interior. But when your rulers are your worst, your wealthy are your stingiest, and your affairs are left to your women, then the interior of the earth is better for you than its surface."

Know that this surah is called Surat al-Shura.

And His saying: ﴿and from what We have provided them, they spend﴾, meaning: they give charity.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who, when tyranny (al-baghy) afflicts them, they defend themselves (yantasirun)﴾. That is: the wrongdoing (al-zulm). His saying: ﴿yantasirun﴾ means: they help one another (yatanasarun), so that some of them support others in removing tyranny. This is from the category of hisbah (enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong), they defend themselves by enjoining the good (al-amr bil-ma'ruf). It has also been said: ﴿yantasirun﴾ means: they take retribution from the wrongdoer, and intisar (retribution) from the wrongdoer is taking the right from him.

In the tafsir it is related from al-Hasan al-Basri and others that he said: "They disliked to humiliate themselves, so that the wicked would not dare to attack them."

Al-Kalbi mentioned that the verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. It is narrated that a man from the Ansar insulted Abu Bakr in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ). Abu Bakr remained silent, and the Prophet (ﷺ) remained silent. Then Abu Bakr responded to him. The Prophet (ﷺ) stood up angrily and left, and Abu Bakr followed him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what you did to me is worse than what the Ansari did. He insulted me and you did not object when I remained silent; then when I answered, you stood up angry." He said: "An angel was responding on his behalf while he remained silent; when you answered, the angel departed, so I left." Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse: ﴿And those who, when tyranny afflicts them, they defend themselves﴾. Therefore it is permissible for the wronged person to take retribution against his oppressor.

The second clause of the verse: "And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it." He named the second "evil" (sayyi'ah) for the sake of verbal parallelism (izdiwaj al-kalam). According to the jurists, the verse concerns killing and wounding: if someone kills, his guardian (waliyy) kills him; and if someone wounds, he is wounded. A group of the early generation (al-salaf) held that this applies also to other than killing and wounding. So if he says, "May God disgrace you," he says, "May God disgrace you," and does not add to it; and if he says, "May God curse you," he says, "May God curse you," and does not exceed it. Likewise, they said: if he insults him, he insults him in return. This applies to what does not involve falsehood; as for what involves falsehood, one should not lie about him. What we have mentioned is related from Mujahid and others.

His words: "But whoever forgives and makes reconciliation, his reward is with God" (﴿فمن عفا وأصلح فأجره على الله﴾), meaning: he pardons the wrongdoer and sets things right between himself and him. "His reward is with God" means: his recompense is with God.

In some reports: "God, the Exalted, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'Let whoever has his reward with God arise,' and none arises except those who pardoned."

His words: "Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers" (﴿إنه لا يحب الظالمين﴾), meaning: those who transgress beyond the right to what is not right.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever avenges himself after being wronged, those—there is no path (of blame) against them﴾, meaning: no path against them on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 42:

And His saying: ﴿The blame is only upon those who wrong people and transgress upon the earth without right﴾ — meaning: they seek an increase that is not theirs. It was also said: they strive upon the earth through acts of disobedience.

And His saying: ﴿For those there is a painful punishment﴾ — meaning: painful, afflicting.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 43:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever endures patiently and forgives﴾, meaning: he endures patiently over harm and forgives the one who harms him. It is also said: he endures patiently against sins and forgives the one who wrongs him. It is also said: he endures patiently against the wronging of people, and whoever wrongs him, he pardons him.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring resolve﴾, meaning: it is of the rights of (the matters). It is also said: it is of the firm resolutions of God which He urged His servants to. It is also said: it is of the established matters that are not abrogated. Al-Zajjaj said: God, may He be exalted, urged the wronged party to pardon the wrongdoer and to endure patiently against the wrong, so that he may attain reward in the Hereafter. Whoever is more eager for the reward of the Hereafter is more resolute in patience.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 44:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And whoever Allah sends astray, for him there is no protector after Him.﴾ That is: Allah misguides him.

And His saying: ﴿for him there is no protector after Him.﴾ That is: he will not find, after Allah, anyone who can guide him.

And His saying: ﴿And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying: "Is there any way to return?"﴾ That is: a return to the world, so that they may repent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 45:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And you will see them being exposed to it﴾ means: to the Fire. It is said that the verse refers to the family of Pharaoh, and it is said that it refers to the family of Pharaoh and others. The more sound view is that this is about the Day of Resurrection, and they will be exposed to the Fire in order to enter it.

And His words: ﴿humbled from [the] humiliation﴾ mean: submissive out of humiliation. Its meaning is [brokenness] and the abasement of the self when they see the punishment and regret befalls them.

His words: ﴿they look from a hidden glance﴾ mean: they steal glances at the Fire. It is said: they look with half of their eyes, and do not open their eyes fully upon it out of fear of it. It is related from some of them that he said: they look with their hearts, because they will be gathered blind, so the "hidden glance" is the sight of the heart.

And His words: ﴿And those who believed will say, "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection."﴾ As for their losing themselves, it is by their entering the Fire; as for their losing their families, it is because, had they believed, they would have obtained families in Paradise, but when they disbelieved and entered the Fire, their families in Paradise were lost to them, so this is the loss of family. It is also said: for each disbeliever there is a named family in Paradise who would have been his had he believed.

And His words: ﴿Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in an enduring punishment﴾ mean: lasting.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 46:

His saying: ﴿And they will have no protectors to help them against Allah﴾, meaning: they will not be able to shield them from the punishment of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no way﴾, meaning: no path to Paradise.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 47:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Respond to your Lord﴾ mean: respond to your Lord by saying: "There is no god but Allah; Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

And His words: ﴿before there comes a Day for which there is no turning back from Allah﴾ mean: there is no repelling of it.

And His words: ﴿You will have no refuge that Day﴾ mean: no escape and no shelter.

And His words: ﴿and you will have no denial﴾ mean: no denial (inkar). It is said: you will have no way to deny the punishment that befalls you. It is also said: ﴿you will have no denial﴾ means: no change (taghyir).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 48:

And His Exalted saying: ﴿But if they turn away, We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾ means: a guardian (ḥafīẓ).

And His saying: ﴿Your duty is only to convey (the message)﴾ means: the conveying (al-tablīgh).

And His saying: ﴿And when We let mankind taste mercy from Us﴾ means: blessing and well-being (al-ni'mah wa'l-'āfiyah).

And His saying: ﴿they rejoice in it﴾ means: they are glad in it.

And His saying: ﴿But if an evil befalls them﴾ means: hardship and affliction. It was also said: drought, which is the opposite of fertility (al-khiṣb).

And His saying: ﴿because of what their hands have put forward﴾ means: because of sins.

And His saying: ﴿indeed, mankind is ungrateful﴾ its meaning: disbelieving in the blessings of Allah, not thanking them.

Allah's words: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows females upon whom He wills, and He bestows males upon whom He wills﴾. That is: He gives females without males, and males without females.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 50:

And His saying: ﴿or He gives them males and females﴾ means: He combines males and females in the bestowal. The meaning of His saying ﴿He gives them [in marriage]﴾ is: He classifies them, as if He makes the offspring into two kinds: a kind of females and a kind of males.

And His saying: ﴿and He makes whomever He wills barren﴾ means: he will have no offspring at all. It is said in the tafsir that the verse concerns the prophets. His saying ﴿He bestows females upon whomever He wills﴾ refers to the Prophet Lot (peace be upon him), who had daughters and had no male offspring. His saying ﴿and He bestows males upon whomever He wills﴾ refers to Ibrahim (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), who had sons and had no daughter. His saying ﴿or He gives them males and females﴾ refers to the Messenger (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), who had four sons and four daughters. The sons: al-Qasim, by whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given his kunya, and Abd Allah, al-Tahir, who was also called al-Tayyib, and Ibrahim. The first three were from Khadijah (may Allah be pleased with her), and Ibrahim was the son of Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah. As for the daughters: Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, and Fatimah, all of them from Khadijah (may Allah be pleased with her and them). His saying ﴿and He makes whomever He wills barren﴾ refers to Yahya and Isa (peace be upon them both), who had neither offspring nor wife.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 51:

The words of the Most High: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation﴾. Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir that the occasion of revelation of this verse was that the polytheists said to the Prophet: "Why does Allah not speak to you and you see Him as Moses did?" So Allah the Most High sent down this verse.

As for His words: ﴿except by revelation﴾, there are two opinions concerning it. The first is that it is inspiration (ilham) from Allah the Most High by a breathing into the heart. The second is that it is a vision in sleep. In some narrations from Ibn 'Abbas: "Among the prophets, Jibril was seen by only four: Musa, 'Isa, Zakariyya, and Muhammad, upon them be blessings and peace. As for the rest, they had revelation and inspiration only." This is a strange report.

As for His words: ﴿or from behind a veil﴾, that is, as Allah spoke to Musa from behind a veil. It was said: the veil is over the place of speech, not over Allah. [And it was said]: when Musa, peace be upon him, heard the speech of Allah without seeing Him, he was in the position of one who hears from behind a veil.

As for His words: ﴿or send a messenger, so he reveals by His permission what He wills﴾, meaning: He sends Jibril with the revelation to whomever He wills of the prophets. [The totality] of what reached the prophets of revelation is in three aspects: inspiration, vision in sleep, and revelation through Allah the Most High's speaking, and revelation through the tongue of Jibril, peace be upon him. It is reported from Mujahid that he said: Allah revealed the Zabur to Dawud, and he recited it from his heart, and it was not on the tongue of Jibril. In some reports: Allah the Most High entrusted Jibril, peace be upon him, with guarding the revelation, and likewise with conveying it to the prophets, and likewise entrusted him with supporting the prophets and punishing the disbelievers. He entrusted Mika'il with rain and plants, entrusted Israfil with the Trumpet, and he is also among the bearers of the Throne, and entrusted the Angel of Death with seizing souls. They are thus charged with these matters by the permission of Allah the Most High.

In some reports, Jibril, peace be upon him, would meet the Prophet in white garments wrapped in pearls and rubies, and his feet were immersed in green. We have mentioned in a narration from the Prophet that "the messengers among the prophets were three hundred and [five] fifteen [in a great multitude]; the first of them was Adam ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾, and the last of them was Muhammad, upon them both be peace."

As for His words: ﴿Indeed He is Most High, Most Wise﴾, that is: exalted above what they (the polytheists) attribute to Him, Wise in all that He does.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 42, verse 52:

Allah's words: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command.﴾ The "spirit" (al-ruh) here is the Qur'an. He called it a spirit because hearts are given life by it just as souls are given life by the spirit. It is also said that it is prophethood, but the first view is more well-known.

His words: ﴿of Our command﴾ mean: by Our command.

His words: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾ The Book is the Qur'an. It is also said: "You did not know what the Book was, had We not sent it down to you." His words: ﴿nor faith﴾ are commonly understood to mean the legal obligations of faith (shara'i' al-iman), and this has been reported from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzayma and others among the imams of the Sunnah.

It is also reported from some of them that its meaning is: "You did not know what the Book was, nor faith," i.e., before puberty. A third view: "You did not know what the Book was, nor faith," i.e., the people of faith; this has been reported from al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Bajali.

In some of the musnads, through the narration of al-Nazzal ibn Sabra from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: "It was said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'Did you ever worship an idol?' He said: 'No.' It was said to him: 'Did you ever drink wine?' He said: 'No.' And I always knew that what they were upon was false, and he was not revealed the Book nor faith." The report is strange (gharib).

His words: ﴿But We made it a light by which We guide whomever We will of Our servants. And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ meaning: you call (to it). In the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "And indeed, you call to a straight path," which clarifies the meaning of the well-known recitation. ʿAsim al-Jahdari recited: "And indeed, you are guided to a straight path" in the passive form (ʿala ma lam yusamma fa'iluh), and its meaning is clear.

The Exalted said: ﴿The path of God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Unquestionably, to God all matters are returned.﴾ That is: all matters return (to Him). And God knows best.
